div.head: II Cn 77
div.ab: ⁊ se man, þe ætfleo fram his hlaforde oððe fram his geferan for his yrhþe, si hit on scipfyrde, si hit on landfyrde, þolige ealles þæs þe he age ⁊ his agenes feores; ⁊ fo se hlaford to þam æhtan ⁊ to his lande, þe he him ær sealde.

Be ðam þe flihð fram his laforde. And ðe man, ðe fleo fram his hlaforde oððe fram his geferan for his yrhðe, sy hit on scypfyrde, sy hit on landfyrde, ðolie he ealles ðæs ðe he age ⁊ his agenes feores; ⁊ fo se hlaford to ðam æhton ⁊ to his lande, ðe he him ær sealde.

And se man, þe ætfleo fram his hlaforde oððe fram his gefearam for his yrhðe, sy hit on scypfyrde, sy hit on landferde, þolige ealles þæs þe he age ⁊ his agenes feores; ⁊ fo se hlaford to þam ehtan ⁊ to his lande, þe he him ær sealde.
Et qui fugiet a domino uel socio suo pro timiditate in expeditione nauali uel terrestri, perdat omne quod suum est et suam ipsius uitam; et manus mittat dominus ad terram, quam ei antea dederat.

Si quis timore perterritus a domino suo aut a sociis suis fugerit de bello siue in terra sive in mari (aqua), careat omnium bonorum suorum cum uita; et dominus (suus) accipiat omnia que illius sunt et terram, si quam ei antea dedisset.

[77] Si quis propter formidolositatem fugiens, dominum uel socium destituerit siue nauali bello siue terrestri, . . . quicquid possidet cum propria uita; terra autem et mobilia cadant in iura et possessionem domini sui.

Be ðam þe flihð fram his laforde. And ðe man ðe fleo fram his hlaforde oððe fram his geferan for his yrhðe, sy hit on scypfyrde, sy hit on landfyrde, ðolie he ealles ðæs ðe he age ⁊ his agenes feores, ⁊ fo se hlaford to ðam æhton ⁊ to his lande ðe he him ær sealde.

And se man þe ætfleo fram his hlaforde oððe fram his geferan for his yrhþe, si hit on scipfyrde, si hit on landfyrde, þolige ealles þæs þe he age and his agenes feores; and fo se hlaford to þam æhtan and to his lande þe he him ær sealde.

(Von dem der von seinem Herrn flieht. B) Und der Mann, welcher durch seine Feigheit entflieht von seinem Herrn oder seinen(-em?) Gefährten, sei es im Schiffsheer, sei es in der Landwehr, verliere alles, was er besitzt und sein eigenes Leben; und greife der Herr zu den Habseligkeiten und dém Lande desselben, das er ihm vorher gegeben hatte.

(Of him who flees from his lord. B) And the man who through his cowardice flees from his lord or his companions (companion?), whether in the ship-army or in the land-army, let him lose all that he possesses and his own life; and let the lord take possession of his goods and of the land which he had previously given him.

Concerning the man who deserts his lord. And the man who, through cowardice, deserts his lord or his comrades on an expedition, either by sea or by land, shall lose all that he possesses and his own life, and the lord shall take back the property and the land which he had given him.

And the man, who in his cowardice deserts his lord or his comrades, whether it is on an expedition by sea or on one on land, is to forfeit all that he owns and his own life; and the lord is to succeed to the possessions and to the land which he previously gave him.

And the man who abandons his lord or his comrades on a campaign out of cowardice, whether on sea or land, shall forfeit all that he possesses and his own life, and his lord shall confiscate all the property and land that he had previously given to him.

Cf. Gl Heer 8eff.; Herrenverrat 7b. c. Perhaps the historical acts of treachery under Æthelred II and Eadmund II gave rise to Cnut's severity. See, however, above 64⁵

QC verstehen Sing.; auf diesen deutet die Endung -an in älterer Sprache. Gemäss jüngerer Sprache ist Plural, den Inst versteht, möglich. Jedenfalls denkt Cnut nicht an nur Einen Gefährten im wörtlichen Sinne; wenn er sich so ausdrückte, so bed., wie oft, der Einzelne die ganze Klasse; vgl. collegam im Gl Heer 8e

QC understand a singular; the ending -an points to this in the older language. In accordance with the later language a plural, as Inst understands it, is possible. In any case Cnut is not thinking of only a single companion in the literal sense; if he expressed himself so, the individual, as often, stands for the whole class; cf. collegam in Gl Heer 8e
Vgl. Gl Schiff 2—6; Vermögenseinziehung 10. d; Todesstrafe 3f
Cf. Gl Schiff 2—6; Vermögenseinziehung 10. d; Todesstrafe 3f
Ebd. Læn 4f. g. Unter den Lateinern lässt Q die Fahrhabe fort und C die Herkunft vom Herrn. Die ganze Fahrhabe lässt Inst dem Herrn zufallen: wie bei Herrenverrat; s. d. 5
Ibid. Læn 4f. g. Of the Latin translators, Q omits the chattels and C the derivation from the lord. Inst makes all the chattels fall to the lord, as in treason against one's lord; see that word 5
Cf. V Atr. 28; VI, 35; Wulfstan, p. 275.
